understood.topic: The principle of inertia (Newton's first law)

answer.title: The principle of inertia (Newton's first law)
answer.summary: If the forces acting on an object cancel out, the object either stays at rest or keeps moving in a straight line at a constant speed.

segments.text: The principle of inertia says an object does not change its motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
When a bus brakes suddenly, your body tends to keep moving forward — that is inertia.
A seat belt provides the force that stops your body together with the car.
In everyday life there is always friction and air resistance, so it is hard to observe uniform straight-line motion for long.

connections.relation: Explains what happens when the forces do not cancel out.
A force that slows objects down, which is why things stop in everyday life.
Seat belts and airbags protect against the effects of inertia.

simplify.title: Inertia in simple words
simplify.text: Objects are "lazy": if they are still, they want to stay still, and if they are moving, they want to keep moving the same way — until a force changes that.
caveats: "Lazy" is only a comparison; objects do not have a will.

examples.title: The bus
examples.body: When the bus starts suddenly, you feel pushed backwards.

examples.title: The tablecloth trick
examples.body: If you pull a tablecloth very quickly, the cups on it can stay in place.

questions.question: An object moves at constant speed in a straight line. What can we say?

choices.text: A large force is pushing it

questions.explanation: According to the principle of inertia, the forces are balanced.

questions.question: Why do we wear a seat belt?

choices.text: So it stops us together with the car when braking

questions.explanation: The seat belt provides the force that stops the body.

questions.question: Why does a rolling ball eventually stop on the ground?

choices.text: Because the principle of inertia is wrong

questions.explanation: Friction is a force that slows the ball down.
